% A whole paper in twenty-odd lines, carrying four properties on purpose.
% Everything a build needs BEYOND the paper — a runner file, .gitignore, git
% init, the agent-set install — is staging and is made by whatever stands this
% up. Only the source belongs here.
%
% PROPERTY 1 — a colon in the title. A YAML emitter must quote a scalar
% containing ": ", so `\title{... : ...}` reaches the rendering's metadata block
% as `title: "Mary and Her Lamb: An Account"`. A reader that keeps the quotes
% carries them into the volume's heading, its directory slug and its
% entry-point link text — and quoted link text is the citation gate's own
% excerpt grammar, so the build died at `graph-init` reporting a
% citation-grammar violation that named nothing resembling a title. Subtitled
% titles are ordinary; no other fixture happens to carry one, which is the only
% reason this never fired. Do not remove the colon.
%
% PROPERTY 2 — no claim-bearing environment anywhere. No \newtheorem, no boxed
% result, nothing the inventory classifies as stating one. A corpus that
% declares no results at all is a legitimate build with an empty claim graph,
% and no other fixture covers it.
%
% PROPERTY 3 — the paper cites. This is load-bearing and is not decoration: an
% uncited bibliography exercises nothing, because no `Cite` node is produced and
% neither the citeproc path nor the filter path is ever reached. The \cite below
% is what makes the three citation states reachable from this one paper.
%
% PROPERTY 4 — two bibliography forms travel beside this file, and BOTH are
% wanted. `lamb.bib` is bibtex's input, which pandoc resolves through
% `--bibliography`: the citation then renders as author-year prose and the
% volume gains a references leaf. `lamb.bbl` is bibtex's OUTPUT — LaTeX markup,
% only the cited works, already formatted — and is the shape an arXiv tarball
% usually ships instead. Pandoc does not pick a .bbl up from `\bibliography{}`;
% it has to be \input or inlined, which is a staging concern rather than a
% property of this file. Neither form is unused: they are the two halves of the
% same test, and dropping the one that looks inert removes a path.
\documentclass{article}
\title{Mary and Her Lamb: An Account}
\author{A. Nonymous}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\begin{abstract}
We recount the case of Mary, who had a little lamb. No results are claimed.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
Mary had a little lamb. Its fleece was white as snow.

\section{Field Observations}
Everywhere that Mary went, the lamb was sure to go. The behaviour is
consistent with earlier accounts of nothing whatsoever \cite{nobody2026}.

\subsection{The Schoolhouse Incident}
It followed her to school one day, which was against the rule.

\subsection{Reception}
It made the children laugh and play to see a lamb at school.

\section{Discussion}
The teacher turned it out, but still it lingered near.

\section{Conclusion}
It waited patiently about till Mary did appear.
\end{document}
